server.note: ATLAS_EXPERIMENTAL is OPEN on this server, so /object_info shows 79 standard + 4 experimental. The plan's 'expect 79' assumed the default-closed gate; 83 here is correct and not a discrepancy.

findings.claim: All 18 zero-product-evidence standard nodes execute and produce meaningful output.
findings.method: In-process execution of each node's FUNCTION with a synthetic solve/IMAGE and real fixtures, signatures read from INPUT_TYPES rather than assumed.
findings.result: 18/18 ok. No node is broken. Every initial failure in the first pass was a bad probe argument, corrected and re-run.
corrections_made: AtlasVPVisualization takes (image, solve) in that order, not (solve, image).
AtlasSolveFromImage / AtlasConstrainedSolve take an IMAGE tensor, not a path.
AtlasConstrainedSolve needs left+right+vertical groups (aliases x/z/y); two groups is not enough. Solved fx=721.6 once given three.
AtlasUSDCameraLoader needs a real .usda; round-trips correctly against AtlasExportUSD output.
findings.consequence: No DELETE is defensible this cycle. The 15 non-duplicate zero-evidence nodes are HOLD_NEEDS_EVIDENCE: working code with no product consumer, not dead code.

findings.claim: AtlasGroundMask output is bit-identical to AtlasGroundDepthMap output 1 (ground_mask).
findings.method: Both nodes run on the same solve across 5 configurations (default, fx=150, elevated eye 12m, raised target, 640x480); plus near/far varied 1/50 vs 5/500 on GroundDepthMap.
findings.result: bit_identical = True in all 5 cases (np.array_equal). Changing near/far does NOT alter the mask, confirming near/far only drive the colour ramp.
findings.consequence: AtlasGroundMask -> LEGACY_GATE is evidence-backed, not inferred from reading. Replacement: AtlasGroundDepthMap output slot 1.

findings.claim: The staircase sawtooth hang is real, and the proposed Guard A fixes it.
findings.method: Bounded subprocess repro of the exact test fixture (64x64 depth, circular rock at 3m, grid_long_edge=32); then a standalone prototype of pass 1 with and without the same-pass shared-edge guard.
findings.consequence: Guard A validated BEFORE implementation. n_added=11 > 0, so the test's existing assertion still holds after the fix; no xfail needed.

findings.claim: defocus_plate's gather is a genuine memory problem (defect D1).
findings.method: tracemalloc peak on the worktree implementation.
findings.consequence: Band-by-band hat-weight accumulation is required before landing AtlasDefocus, justified by measurement rather than assumption.

findings.claim: PLAN AMENDMENT — the LiveMeshRepair migration is not a 1:1 node swap.
findings.method: Read the widgets and link graph of all three workflows; confirmed node shapes against the live /object_info catalog.

result.AtlasLiveMeshRepair: sweeps the WHOLE solve (every relief mesh, all layers)
result.AtlasPlanarHolePatch: link_inputs [solve, hole_mask]; widget 'layer' targets ONE named source or '' (primary). No '*' option.
result.AtlasCleanPlateLayer: outputs [solve, hole_mask, extend_mask] — hole_mask exists per layer but is currently UNWIRED in both moge workflows
result.atlas_4layer_boundedband_bgcard_moge: named layers: sky (node 10), background (node 11), machine (node 12), foreground (node 13)

findings.consequence: A faithful migration needs ONE AtlasPlanarHolePatch per named layer, each fed that layer's own hole_mask — 2 patches for the 3-layer graph, 3 for the 4-layer graph — then one AtlasRetopologizeLayer(layer='*'). The plan's single-patch chain would have silently repaired only one layer. Alternative worth costing in C4: teach AtlasPlanarHolePatch's existing STRING 'layer' widget to accept '*' (legal — it is a STRING, not a combo), which needs a per-layer mask story.

findings.claim: atlas_live_repair_and_bands_test_workflow.json is already unrunnable on this machine.
findings.result: valid=false, errors=['type PreviewTextNode unknown'] — a third-party node that is not installed.
findings.consequence: Retiring this workflow (plan C4) costs nothing that currently works. Replacing it with atlas_boundary_smooth_retopo_test_workflow.json is a strict improvement.

path_guided_chain.design_note: This workflow is TWO-PASS BY DESIGN and its own Note 11 says so: queue once to build the relief and the conservative first pass, then author an Orbit/Arc in the viewport, then queue again so the path-guided pass has a camera path. A single headless queue therefore exercises only pass 1 — that is correct behaviour, not a defect, and AtlasPathGuidedHoleRepair says exactly what to do ('camera path is empty — choose Orbit/Arc, then queue or bake').

pass_1_only.AtlasPathGuidedHoleRepair: camera path is empty — fail-soft, no selection

with_camera_path.method: synthesised a 15-degree orbit around the solved scene pivot (camera 0,1.6,0; scene depth 30.83 m) and injected it through the viewport's client_data override — the shipped graph, not the -edit copy
with_camera_path.AtlasPathGuidedHoleRepair: path frame 99/99 (offset 0 from end); lens 1.000x; 39 source islands, 31 candidate planes, 12 visible, 12 selected (selection=all_visible); source mask 450033 px; candidate-fit rejections: 2 max_hole_fraction, 6 plane residual
with_camera_path.AtlasPlanarHolePatch_pass2: filled 10/12 attempted (12 found), +511 verts, +1860 faces; 2 rejected on generated patch edge
with_camera_path.conclusion: The path-guided selection stage works end to end on a real plate: it rasterises candidates from the path's final frame, selects the islands visible from that angle, and the second patch pass fills them under its own gates.

arc_orbit_on_machine_plate.plate: atlas_00025.png (7680x4512, the 8K machine plate both moge workflows load)
arc_orbit_on_machine_plate.solve: camera height 1.4505 m, scene depth 44.72 m, fov_h 57.75 deg, scale_source depth_ground_plane (MEASURED, safe_to_export)
arc_orbit_on_machine_plate.camera_path: Arc preset shape — 3 keyframes at 0/60/99, orbit 15 deg about world-Y through the pivot WHILE dollying in 15% (6.091 -> 5.634 -> 5.178 m from pivot), so the Catmull-Rom actually curves. Pivot taken from the artist's own authored path for this same plate, whose eye height 1.450573 matches the solve exactly.

arc_orbit_end_frame.pass1: filled 206/218 attempted (235 found), +911 verts, +5020 faces — identical, as it must be; the arc only affects the second pass
arc_orbit_end_frame.path_guided: path frame 99/99 (offset 0 from end), lens 1.000x; 29 source islands, 25 candidate planes, 13 visible, 13 selected; source mask 511830 px; rejections 1 max_hole_fraction, 3 plane residual
arc_orbit_end_frame.pass2: filled 10/13 attempted (13 found), +368 verts, +1372 faces; accepted edge stretch 36.8x/40.0x, depth excursion 1.13x/2.00x; 3 rejected on generated patch edge

arc_orbit_on_machine_plate.conclusion: The arc adds 368 vertices and 1372 faces of geometry the baseline never produced. The selected islands are a strict SUBSET of the pass-1 remaining holes (29 -> 13 visible -> 10 filled), which is the path-guided stage doing exactly what it claims: repairing only what the chosen camera move will actually reveal.

exclude_mask_polarity_ab.why: The shipping path-guided workflow ships exclude_mask UNWIRED on both AtlasDeriveReliefMesh and AtlasPathGuidedHoleRepair. The artist's local -edit copy wires BiRefNet-HR-matting into both. Ran three arms on atlas_00025.png with one identical arc (15 deg orbit + 15% dolly-in, frames 0/60/99, end frame 99/99) to isolate the mask.
exclude_mask_polarity_ab.mask_polarity_measured: BiRefNet-HR-matting raw MASK = 25.35% of frame = the machine plus the grass slope it stands on. invert_output=True gives the 74.65% complement (sea, sky, far cliffs, left foreground rocks).

A_no_exclude_mask.path: 29 source islands, 25 candidate planes, 13 visible, 13 selected

B_invert_true_artist_wiring.path: 346 source islands, 296 candidate planes, 140 visible, 140 selected; exclude removed 25830731 background/sky hole pixels

C_invert_false_machine_cut.path: 202 source islands, 178 candidate planes, 80 visible, 80 selected; exclude removed 8816145 background/sky hole pixels
C_invert_false_machine_cut.pass2: 78/80, +1235 verts, +3418 faces; 2 rejected on generated patch edge, ZERO plane-fit rejections
C_invert_false_machine_cut.note: Excluding the SUBJECT leaves a machine-shaped hole in the landscape mesh, so the repair fills BEHIND the machine. Best geometry recovery and best hit rate of the three.

findings: exclude_mask unwired is not a neutral default: arm A recovers roughly a third of arm C's pass-2 geometry from the identical camera move.

Polarity is a silent footgun. Both wirings execute clean and report success; only the geometry delta distinguishes excluding the background from excluding the subject. Which polarity is correct depends on whether you are repairing the hero or repairing behind it.

A shipping example cannot depend on BiRefNetRMBG (third-party ComfyUI-RMBG). AtlasSAM3Mask is native and already the preferred segmenter in AtlasInput's sky/scope cascade, so it is the candidate for wiring this in-repo.

sam3_union_replaces_maskcomposite.why: The 2026-07-27 polarity work told artists to OR a subject mask with a sky mask via MaskComposite(add) for repair-behind-the-subject. That advice was unnecessary: AtlasSAM3Mask.concepts is ALREADY a union across every concept.

single_node_union.wiring: one AtlasSAM3Mask, concepts='sky, machinery' -> exclude_mask on both AtlasDeriveReliefMesh and AtlasPathGuidedHoleRepair
single_node_union.exclude_report: covers 54.2% of frame; removed 18786665 hole pixels (90.4% of candidates) — 27.4% sky + 26.8% machinery, unioned
single_node_union.path: 371 source islands, 278 candidate planes, 117 visible, 117 selected

two_mask_composite_it_replaces.verdict: equivalent outcome; the single node drops the third-party ComfyUI-RMBG dependency and one node from the graph

THE_REAL_TRAP_IS_VOCABULARY.finding: SAM3 is open-vocabulary and a miss is SILENT — an empty mask, no error. On this plate the obvious word failed and near-synonyms worked.
THE_REAL_TRAP_IS_VOCABULARY.consequence: concepts='sky, machine' silently yields a SKY-ONLY exclude, turning a repair-behind-the-subject graph back into a repair-the-subject's-own-tears one. The node report naming the matched subset is the only visible signal, so it is now pinned by tests/test_sam3_segmenter.py::test_sam3_mask_node_report_names_the_concepts_that_actually_matched.

sam3_union_replaces_maskcomposite.note: This run was also the first live sighting of the exclude-coverage report line added 2026-07-27 ('exclude mask covers N% of frame'), previously only unit-pinned because the server was running pre-edit modules.
